elements.content: Communication Goal: I can describe my daily routine, tell the time, talk about days, and explain how I travel to work.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 4. Daily routine
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: My daily routine
- Materials: Clock face, routine sequence cards, whiteboard, COSYmanuals 'telling the time' and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• tell time and talk about days
• describe a daily routine
• explain how I travel to work
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles time expressions and present simple.

Next lesson: Lesson 5 recycles routines to talk about habits and questions.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (20 items):

wake up — to stop sleeping. Example: I wake up at seven.
get up — to leave your bed. Example: I get up at seven fifteen.
shower — a wash under falling water. Example: I take a shower every morning.
breakfast — the first meal of the day. Example: I have breakfast at eight.
work — a job or activity you do. Example: I work in an office.
bed — furniture for sleeping. Example: I go to bed at eleven.
o'clock — used to say a full hour. Example: It is seven o'clock.
half past — thirty minutes after the hour. Example: It is half past seven.
monday — the first day of the working week. Example: I start work at nine on Monday.
friday — the last day of the working week. Example: I finish early on Friday.
morning — the early part of the day. Example: I check messages in the morning.
afternoon — the part of the day after midday. Example: I have lunch in the afternoon.
evening — the part of the day before night. Example: I go home in the evening.
night — the dark part of the day. Example: I don't use my phone at night.
commute — to travel to and from work. Example: I commute by metro.
metro — a city train system. Example: I take the metro to work.
bus — a large road vehicle for passengers. Example: She goes by bus.
train — a vehicle that runs on rails. Example: We take the train at eight.
walk — to move on foot. Example: I walk to the station.
on time — not early and not late. Example: I am always on time.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I wake up at seven o'clock. (starting a routine)
• I get up at half past seven. (morning action and time)
• I have breakfast at eight. (meal time)
• I go to work at nine on Monday. (work time and day)
• I take the metro. / I walk. (talking about transport)
• I get off at Central Station. (ending a journey)
• What time do you...? / How do you get to work? (asking about routine and transport)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'to stop sleeping'?
Which word means 'to leave your bed'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Telling-time stress and the /ʃ/ sound in 'shower'

o'clock /əˈklɒk/ — stress the second syllable
half past /hɑːf pɑːst/ — link the words
shower /ˈʃaʊə/ — starts with /ʃ/
breakfast /ˈbrekfəst/ — stress the first syllable

I wake up at seven o'clock. I go to bed at half past ten.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use time expressions to say when you do something.

Form:
Telling the time: What time is it? It's seven o'clock. It's half past seven. It's quarter past seven. It's quarter to eight. Use 'at' + time: at seven o'clock.

Examples:
• I wake up at seven o'clock.
• The class starts at half past nine.
• We have lunch at quarter past twelve.
• She goes to bed at ten o'clock.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
It's 7:00. It's ___ o'clock.
It's 7:30. It's half ___ seven.
It's 7:45. It's quarter ___ eight.
I wake up ___ seven o'clock.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I wake up at ...
• I have breakfast at ...
• I go to bed at ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What time do you wake up?
• What time do you start work or school?
• What time do you go to bed?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your day with times.
• Write three sentences about a family member's day with times.
Reading: My daily routine

I wake up at seven o'clock on Monday. I get up at half past seven and take a shower. I have breakfast at eight. I go to work at nine. I take the metro and get off at Central Station. I start work at half past nine. In the afternoon, I have lunch at one. I finish work at six in the evening. I go to bed at half past ten. On Saturday, I don't work. I usually walk in the park.
What time does the writer wake up?
How does the writer get to work?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What time do you wake up?
B: I wake up at six thirty.
A: And how do you get to work?
B: I take the bus and get off at the park.
A: What time do you start work?
B: At eight o'clock on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.
A: Do you work on Saturday?
B: No, I don't. I relax at home.
How does the speaker get to work?
Does the speaker work on Saturday?
Speaking task: Compare your daily routine and commute with your partner. Find two differences.

• What time do you wake up?
• What do you do on Monday morning?
• How do you get to work or school?
• What do you do in the evening?
• Are you usually on time?
Role-play: You are planning a coffee chat. Compare your weekly schedules and find a free time on Wednesday or Friday.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your weekday routine with times, days, and transport.
Model: I wake up at ... On Monday, I ... I take the ... I get off at ...
